findings.title: Potential SSRF/Path Traversal via URL Normalization Removal
findings.description: Removing URL normalization logic for double-slash paths without verifying downstream safety may reintroduce potential Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) or request smuggling vulnerabilities. While `//` is valid in RFC 3986, stripping leading slashes is a common heuristic to prevent `..%2F` or `//` traversal confusion. Removing this heuristic must be paired with rigorous input validation to prevent path manipulation.
findings.suggestion: Maintain strict URL normalization for proxy requests. Ensure that `//` is not stripped in a way that allows traversal to escape the intended host scope, or add explicit validation against double slashes that could be misinterpreted by the proxy layer.
